name: Dundee Cake
desc: A rich fruit cake with rings of whole almonds on top and never, ever a glace cherry. Dundee's marmalade makers, the Keillers, made it famous. Restores 120 HP.

name: Forfar Bridie
desc: A horseshoe of flaky pastry stuffed with minced beef and onion, from Forfar, just up the road from Dundee. Restores 100 HP and fills you up till teatime.

name: Dundee Marmalade
desc: Thick-cut Seville orange marmalade in a white stoneware jar, the way Keiller's of Dundee sold it round the world. Restores 10 PP to every move.

name: Featherie
desc: An old golf ball: a stitched leather case stuffed with a top hat's worth of boiled goose feathers and hammered round. St Andrews ball makers made them by hand until the cheaper gutta-percha 'gutty' arrived around 1848.

name: Jute Fibre
desc: Golden fibre from Bengal, softened with whale oil and spun in Dundee's mills into sacking, sandbags and the backing for linoleum. Rough on the hands, good for snares.

name: Culross Girdle
desc: A flat iron griddle for baking oatcakes and scones over a fire. In 1599 King James VI gave the hammermen of Culross the sole right to make girdles in Scotland.
